items.actClause: AN ACT to direct the New York state department of health to conduct a study on the high incidence of asthma and related pulmonary disorders in the borough of Brooklyn in the city of New York and to prepare a remedial plan
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5770

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to direct the New York state department of
health to conduct a study on the high incidence of asthma and related
pulmonary disorders in the borough of Brooklyn in the city of New York
and to prepare a remedial plan

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

Purpose of the bill is to conduct a study of the incidence of asthma
and related pulmonary disorders in the borough of Brooklyn in the City
of New York and to provide the Governor and the Legislature with a
remedial plan that addresses the needs of high risk neighborhoods by
examining the inequities in: income, public and private housing, race
and ethnicity, proximity to major sources of air pollution, including
but not limited to, highly trafficked roadways and solid waste
processing facilities, and an evaluation of the effectiveness of
existing medical facilities in the treatment of these pulmonary
disorders.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

This bill directs the Commissioner of the New York State Department of
Health to prepare a remedial plan to address high incidents of asthma
and other pulmonary disorders in the borough of Brooklyn in the city
of New York. The study is to be completed within twelve months of the
effective date of this act.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Asthma alone affects more than one million people in the state of New
York. Recent studies point to a strong connection between high asthma
rates and socioeconomic status, and several Brooklyn neighborhoods
have a far higher rate of emergency room visits and hospitalizations
for asthma and other related pulmonary illnesses.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New Legislation

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the one hundred twentieth day after it
shall have become a law and the results of such study and the remedial
plan shall be provided to the governor and the legislature on later
than eighteen months from the beginning of such study.

VETO MESSAGE - No. 233
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bills:
 
Senate Bill Number 3103, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to direct the New York State Department of Health to conduct
      a  study  on  the  high incidence of asthma in the boroughs of the
      Bronx, Manhattan, and Brooklyn in the city  of  New  York  and  to
      prepare a remedial plan"
 
Senate Bill Number 5559 entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to direct the New York state department of health to conduct
      a  study on the high incidence of asthma in the borough of Manhat-
      tan in the city of New York and to prepare a remedial plan"
 
Senate Bill Number 5770 entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to direct the New York state department of health to conduct
      a study on the high incidence  of  asthma  and  related  pulmonary
      disorders  in  the borough of Brooklyn in the city of New York and
      to prepare a remedial plan"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  These bills would require the State Department of  Health  to  conduct
three separate epdemiological studies related to the incidence of asthma
in  Manhattan,  the  Bronx,  and  Brooklyn. The Department would also be
tasked with implementing remedial plans to address their findings.
 
  The Department is currently implementing a comprehensive  Preventative
Health agenda to make New York the healthiest state in the nation, which
includes  addressing  asthma  in  high incidence districts such as those
identified in the pending bills. Developed in collaboration with  multi-
ple  stakeholders,  the agenda will seek to improve the health status of
all New Yorkers and to reduce health disparities  through  an  increased
emphasis  on  prevention. Although these bills would appear to align the
Department's goals, they do not address the concerns I raised last  year
when I vetoed the same bill for Bronx County. (Veto No. 262 of 2016).
 
  First,  these  bills  focus  solely  on  one-off  local  public health
solutions to combatting asthma, which does not align  with  the  Depart-
ment's  statewide  focus  on  this  issue.  For  example, the Department
currently implements  two  statewide  programs:  the  Children's  Asthma
Program    and  the  Childhood  Asthma Coalitions Program. Through these
programs, the Department conducts outreach and education,  and  develops
and  implements  plans  to  address  asthma's  prevalence throughout the
State.
 
  Second, these bills would require the Department to conduct three  new
studies  without  any  established  funding  source.  These  bills would
require the collection of individual-level data from residents in  three
counties,  as  well  as  an  evaluation of every medical facility in the
Bronx, Manhattan, and Brooklyn to assess and  treat  patients  suffering
from  asthma.  The cost of conducting all three studies and implementing
 
remedial plans is estimated at $3 million. Such funding decisions should
be addressed in the context of the State budget negotiations. For  these
reasons, I am constrained to veto these bills.
 
  These bills are disapproved.                (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
